# Claude Code 101: The workflow that changed how I build features

Whether you're new to Claude Code or feel like you've been using it wrong, you're in the right place.

Most developers approach it the same way:  
\-> "Build feature X,"  
\-> Get messy output  
\-> Conclude the tool isn't ready.  
I was one of them until I fundamentally changed my approach.

Here's the thing about being a developer: you're constantly learning.  
New frameworks, new patterns, new tools. Most bring incremental improvements.  
But every once in a while, something fundamentally reshapes how you work.

Claude Code was that for me.

In this guide, I'll walk you through the workflow that transformed my development process: setting up persistent context, mastering Plan Mode, and configuring specialized subagents.

This isn't an exhaustive exploration of everything Claude Code can do. It's a practical guide focused on what actually works well for me day to day.

Let's dive in. 🤿

## What is Claude Code, really?

Here's the crucial mindset shift: **visualize** **Claude Code as a developer tool**, not a magic box that does everything for you.

It can be incredibly effective when used well. It can also mess up codebases when used poorly. The difference lies entirely in your approach.

## Core principles for success

Three elements make the difference between frustration and flow:

1.  **The claude.md file** for persistent project context
2.  **Plan Mode** for thinking before building
3.  **Specialized subagents** for delegating to the right expert

Get these right, and Claude Code becomes a genuinely powerful part of your toolkit. Let's break them down.

### 1\. A good claude.md file 📄

First thing: set up a `claude.md` file in your project root.  
Think of this as a persistent guide that Claude references on almost every prompt.

What belongs in there?

| Element | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| **Project overview** | What your application does and its core purpose |
| **Tech stack** | Languages, frameworks, key libraries |
| **Architecture patterns** | How your codebase is structured |
| **Coding conventions** | Naming conventions, file organization, preferred patterns |
| **Testing strategy** | How and where tests should be written |
| **Common pitfalls** | Things Claude should avoid based on your project specifics |

The more context here, the less you repeat yourself. Update it as your project evolves.

### 2\. Plan Mode: think before you build 🗺️

With your claude.md in place, you're ready for the next piece of the puzzle: how you actually build features.

This is the cornerstone of using Claude Code properly.

It's tempting to ask Claude to "implement feature X" directly. Don't.

For complex features, this rarely works well. The code might function, but it lacks coherence with your existing architecture.

**Why?** When you jump straight to implementation, Claude makes assumptions about your architecture, naming conventions, and patterns. These assumptions compound. You end up with code that technically works but feels foreign to your codebase.

**The fix: Plan Mode.**

Toggle it by pressing `Shift + Tab` twice. Describe the feature you want in detail. Claude will analyze your codebase and draft a structured plan.

Here's the key: read that plan carefully. Iterate on it. Ask Claude to break it down into ordered implementation tasks. This step is where you save hours of refactoring later.

### 3\. Specialized subagents 🤖

Once you have a solid plan, here's where things get really powerful: specialized subagents.

These handle different parts of your codebase. Each subagent operates in its own context window, keeping your main conversation clean and focused.

Think of them as specialized team members. You wouldn't ask your backend developer to handle your design system. Same logic here.

**Common configurations:**

| Agent | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| **Frontend agent** | Component library, styling conventions, state management |
| **Backend agent** | API design, database schema, authentication flows |
| **Testing agent** | Coverage, edge cases, quality assurance |
| **Documentation agent** | READMEs, API docs, inline comments |
| **Architecture agent** | Structural decisions, consistency |

**How to set up subagents**

Setting up subagents is straightforward. Run `/agents` in Claude Code to open the management interface. From there you can create new agents at project level (stored in `.claude/agents/`) or user level (stored in `~/.claude/agents/`).

Each subagent is a Markdown file with YAML frontmatter:

```markdown
---
name: frontend dev
description: Frontend specialist. Use for React components, styling, and state management.
tools: Read, Edit, Bash, Grep, Glob
model: sonnet
---

You are a frontend expert specializing in React and TypeScript.

When invoked:
1. Review the component requirements
2. Check existing patterns in the codebase
3. Implement following established conventions
4. Ensure proper typing and error handling

Focus on clean, maintainable component architecture.
```

**Pro tip**: Let Claude generate the initial subagent for you, then customize it. Run `/agents`, select "Create New Agent," and describe what you need. Claude will draft the configuration. You refine from there.

The `description` field matters. Make it specific and action oriented. Include phrases like "Use proactively" if you want Claude to invoke it automatically when relevant.

## The full development workflow

Now that you understand the three core elements, let's see how they work together. This is the workflow I follow for every feature I build:

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                     CLAUDE CODE WORKFLOW                        │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                              │
                              ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  1. SETUP                                                       │
│     claude.md + subagents + MCP (Linear/Jira)                   │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                              │
                              ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  2. PLAN MODE (Shift+Tab x2)                                    │
│     Describe feature → Claude analyzes codebase → Draft plan    │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                              │
                              ▼
                    ┌─────────────────┐
                    │  Plan looks     │
                    │  good?          │◄──────────────┐
                    └─────────────────┘               │
                      │           │

# How to Use Claude Code: A Step-by-Step Beginner’s Guide (2026)

![](https://howtoai.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/David-Davis-Cartoon-150x150.png.webp)By [David Davis](https://howtoai.com/about/ "View all posts by David Davis")

![Young woman at a laptop with a friendly robot assistant pointing at a floating code panel](https://howtoai.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/how-to-use-claude-code-banner.jpg)

To use Claude Code, install it with one command, open a terminal in your project folder, type `claude` and sign in with a paid Claude plan (Pro, Max, Team or Enterprise) or a Claude Console account. Then describe what you want in plain English: Claude reads your files, makes or proposes the changes and runs commands, while you review, steer or rewind as it works.

This guide takes you through it in order: which plan you need, the install command for your system, your first session, the CLAUDE.md file that gives Claude a memory, the permission modes that decide what Claude can do without asking, plan mode, the commands worth learning first, safety, cost control and fixes for the most common problems. Every command and setting below was checked against Anthropic’s own Claude Code documentation.

## Claude Code at a glance

|     |     |
| --- | --- |
| What it is | Anthropic’s agentic coding tool: it reads your codebase, edits files, runs commands and works with git |
| Where it runs | Terminal (CLI), VS Code and Cursor, JetBrains IDEs, the Claude desktop app (Code tab), the web at claude.ai/code and the Claude mobile app |
| Plans that include it | Pro, Max, Team and Enterprise. The Free plan does not include it |
| Pay-as-you-go option | A Claude Console account with prepaid API credits, billed at API rates |
| Install on macOS, Linux, WSL | `curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh \| bash` |
| Install on Windows (PowerShell) | `irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 \| iex` |
| Start a session | Open a terminal in your project folder and run `claude` |
| Starting permission mode | Auto mode for terminal and VS Code sessions on v2.1.283 or later. Press Shift+Tab to switch |
| Project memory | A CLAUDE.md file in your project. Run `/init` to create one |
| Undo | Press Esc twice or run `/rewind` to restore code and conversation to an earlier point |

_Checked against Anthropic’s Claude Code documentation, the claude.com pricing page and the Claude Help Center on October 8, 2026._

## What is Claude Code?

Claude Code is Anthropic’s agentic coding tool. Unlike a chat window where you paste code back and forth, it works directly in your project: it reads the files it needs, edits them, runs commands such as your tests or git, and checks the results. Instead of writing the code and asking for a review, you describe the outcome and Claude explores, plans and implements it.

It runs in several places. They all use the same engine, so your CLAUDE.md files, settings and MCP servers carry over between them:

*   **Terminal (CLI):** the full-featured version. Everything in this guide works here.
*   **VS Code and Cursor:** an extension with inline diffs, @-mentions and plan review. It needs VS Code 1.94.0 or later.
*   **JetBrains IDEs:** a plugin for IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm and others. It needs the CLI installed separately.
*   **Desktop app:** the Code tab in the Claude app for macOS and Windows, with Linux in beta. It includes Claude Code, so there is no terminal or separate install.
*   **Web and mobile:** cloud sessions at claude.ai/code or in the Claude app for iOS and Android. Claude clones a GitHub repository into an Anthropic-managed virtual machine, does the work and pushes a branch for you to review.

Never used a terminal? Anthropic’s [terminal guide](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/terminal-guide) shows how to open one and paste a command, and the desktop app skips the terminal entirely. Still choosing a tool? See [ChatGPT vs Claude vs Gemini](https://howtoai.com/chatgpt-vs-claude-vs-gemini/) or [which AI tool you should use](https://howtoai.com/which-ai-tool-should-i-use/). For the non-coding side of Claude, see [the parts of Claude most people never find](https://howtoai.com/claude-ai-hidden-features/).

## Which Claude plans include Claude Code?

Claude Code is included in every paid Claude plan, from Pro up. The Free plan does not include it. You can also skip the subscription and pay per use through a Claude Console account.

| Plan | Price (USD, before tax) | Claude Code |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Free | $0  | Not included |
| Pro | $20 a month, or $17 a month billed annually ($200 a year) | Included |
| Max | From $100 a month, for 5x or 20x the usage of Pro | Included |
| Team | Standard seat $25 a month ($20 billed annually); premium seat $125 ($100 billed annually) with 5x the usage of a standard seat | Included with every seat |
| Enterprise | $20 per seat a month billed annually, plus usage at API rates | Included with the Enterprise seat on new and self-serve plans |
| Claude Console (API) | Prepaid API credits, billed at standard API rates | Pay as you go |

_Prices from claude.com/pricing on October 8, 2026. On older Enterprise plans, Claude Code comes only with Chat + Claude Code or Premium seats._

**Your limits are shared.** On Pro and Max, Claude and Claude Code draw on the same usage limits: a five-hour session limit and a weekly limit. Chatting in the Claude app and coding in the terminal count against the same pool, and Claude Code warns you as you get close. At the limit you can wait for the reset, upgrade, turn on usage credits or switch to Console API credits.

**Watch for a stray API key.** If an `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` environment variable is set and you approve it when Claude Code asks, the session bills that key at API rates instead of using your subscription. Run `/status` in a session to see which account it is using.

### Can you use Claude Code for free?

Not on the Free plan. The cheapest ways in are Pro at $20 a m
